title: Cut Out the Middle Node
statement:
You get the head of a singly linked list with n nodes. Remove its middle node and return the head of the shortened list.

Counting positions from 0, the middle node is at index ⌊n / 2⌋. For an even length that is the second of the two central nodes. A list with one node becomes empty.

examples.why: n = 4, so index 2: the second of the two central nodes, not the first.
The only node is the middle one.

hints: To unlink a node you need the node just before it. Which index is that?
Counting the length in one pass and walking to index ⌊n/2⌋ − 1 in a second pass works. Can you find that node in one walk?
Move a slow pointer one step and a fast pointer two steps, but give the fast pointer a head start of two nodes, so slow stops right before the middle.

explain.intuition:
Deleting from a singly linked list means rewiring the previous node: prev.next = prev.next.next. So the real task is landing on the node before the middle.

The fast/slow trick finds the middle in one walk: when the fast pointer, moving two steps at a time, reaches the end, the slow one is halfway. Starting fast two nodes ahead (at head.next.next) shifts slow back by one, so it stops exactly before index ⌊n/2⌋. A one-node list has no previous node and simply becomes empty.
steps: If the list has a single node, return an empty list.
While fast and fast.next exist, move slow one step and fast two steps.
pitfalls: Deleting the first of the two central nodes for an even length. [1, 2, 3, 4] loses the 3, not the 2.
Stopping slow on the middle node. In a singly linked list you cannot remove a node without its predecessor.
Forgetting the single-node list, where head.next.next does not exist.

solutions.title: Count, then walk
solutions.idea: Measure the length, walk to index ⌊n/2⌋ − 1, and unlink the next node.

solutions.title: Fast and slow pointers
solutions.idea: Start fast two nodes ahead, so when it runs off the end, slow sits just before the middle.

followups: Remove the first of the two central nodes instead when the length is even. Which start position changes?
Remove the middle node when you are handed only a reference to that node, not the head.
lcTitle: Delete the Middle Node of a Linked List
